observation: A two-storey detached house with a steep roof: two slopes meet at a ridge and each end wall rises to a triangle. Red clay roof tiles. The walls are red brick.
A six-storey apartment block with a flat roof edged by a low parapet. The facade is smooth grey concrete with regular windows.
A single-storey bungalow whose roof slopes down on all four sides to the eaves. Dark grey shingles. White painted walls.
A small modern studio with one roof plane tilted from a tall front wall down to a low back wall. Dark metal roofing. The walls are clad in vertical black timber.
A three-storey townhouse painted ochre yellow, with a pitched roof whose ridge runs parallel to the street and gable ends facing the neighbours. Brown roof tiles.
A glass-and-steel office tower of roughly twenty floors with a flat roof crowned by mechanical equipment. Blue-tinted glass curtain wall.
The photo shows a busy crossroads with cars and pedestrians; buildings are only blurred shapes at the edges of the frame.
A four-storey building with cream render. The roof cannot be seen from street level because of the angle.
A pink-painted two-storey cottage with a pyramid-shaped roof rising to a single point from all four sides. Red tiles.
An old stone church built from beige sandstone, about three storeys tall to the eaves, with a steep two-sided roof and gable ends. The roof is covered in green copper.
A long terrace of identical houses; the one in the middle is two storeys of red brick with a dark slate roof that has two slopes meeting at a ridge.
A five-storey Haussmann-style building in pale limestone with a mansard roof of dark grey zinc that slopes on all sides.
A low supermarket, one storey, with a flat roof covered in light grey gravel. Terracotta-coloured panels on the walls.
An interior photo of a café: tables, a counter, and a window. No building exterior is visible.
